binders: Arbitrary types Direction, Cell, and E, with E an additive commutative group and a real module.
An abstract grid on Direction and Cell.
A family methods assigning a directional numerical method to every direction.
A list directionOrder specifying the order of directional updates.
In the concrete conjunct, grid functions U : Int × Int → Real.
hypotheses: For every direction d, the direction stored in methods(d) is d.
directionOrder is a permutation of the grid's coordinate-direction list.

The grid structure itself carries proofs that its coordinate directions are duplicate-free, that two distinct coordinate directions exist, and that its left and right neighbor maps are mutual inverses.
Each directional method itself carries positivity of its time-step-over-cell-width coefficient and consistency of its numerical flux with its physical flux.
conclusions: For every abstract instance satisfying the stated hypotheses, the grid geometry is one of the two geometry constructors.
The coordinate-direction list has no duplicates and contains two distinct directions.
Every grid coordinate direction occurs in directionOrder; its selected method stores that same direction and has a strictly positive time-step-over-cell-width coefficient.
For every direction d, state U, and cell c, the one-direction update is U(c) - λ_d(F_d(U(c),U(right_d(c))) - F_d(U(left_d(c)),U(c))).
Every one-direction update preserves every constant state.
The split update is exactly the left-to-right sequential composition of the one-direction updates in directionOrder.

For the concrete integer-pair grid, Boolean directions [false, true], coefficient-one left-state flux methods, and that order, the split advance sends every U to the diagonal shift (i,j) ↦ U(i-1,j-1).
On the state U(i,j) = real(i)·real(j), this concrete split advance is not equal as a function to the reference operator U(i-1,j) + U(i,j-1) - U(i,j).
mathematical_definitions: One-direction advance: A_d(U)(c) = U(c) - λ_d(F_d(U(c),U(right_d(c))) - F_d(U(left_d(c)),U(c))).
Sequential composition: apply the mapped operators in list order by a left fold; for [false, true], apply the false-direction update first and the true-direction update second.
Concrete false-direction neighbors change only the first integer coordinate by ±1; concrete true-direction neighbors change only the second coordinate by ±1.
Concrete numerical flux: F(left,right) = left, with coefficient λ = 1 and physical flux equal to the identity.
Concrete additive reference: R(U)(i,j) = U(i-1,j) + U(i,j-1) - U(i,j).
Exactness on a family means equality of the split and reference advances for every state in that family; disagreement means inequality of the resulting states for one specified input state.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The proposition combines an abstract bookkeeping theorem with a concrete calculation. Abstractly, any well-formed grid and consistent family of directional numerical methods, ordered by a permutation of the grid directions, satisfy the explicitly stated geometry, direction, positivity, conservative-update, constant-preservation, and sequential-composition properties. Concretely, on the integer lattice with the two coordinate directions, unit coefficient, and a numerical flux that returns its left input, applying the two directional updates in the order false then true shifts every grid function diagonally to U(i-1,j-1). Nevertheless, on the bilinear coordinate-product state Q(i,j)=ij, that split result is not the same function as the additive reference Q(i-1,j)+Q(i,j-1)-Q(i,j).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The abstract portion is conditional on being given both a direction-matching proof and a permutation proof; for choices where such proofs cannot be supplied, it makes no assertion.
Many abstract conclusions restate data or proofs already stored in the grid or method structures, or unfold definitions; consequently that portion has limited independent mathematical content.
The geometry disjunction is exhaustive because the geometry type has the two listed constructors, so it does not impose a substantive geometric classification beyond the encoded datatype.
The exactness claim uses the universal set, whose membership condition is always true; it is therefore genuinely universal over all concrete grid functions rather than vacuous.
The final disagreement is inequality of two functions, which logically requires only one point of disagreement; it is not itself phrased as pointwise inequality at every cell.
No stability, convergence, error estimate, boundary condition, finite-domain restriction, or upper CFL-type bound is asserted; only strict positivity of the coefficient appears.
The concrete result depends on the fixed order [false, true], although the two coordinate shifts commute in this particular construction.
ambiguities: The two geometry constructors have no supplied mathematical labels, so they can only be described as the two constructor alternatives.
The intended domain-specific names of the abstract grid, numerical method, split advance, and reference operators are hidden by local identifiers.
The proposition does not explain why the additive reference operator is the comparison of interest or what broader numerical claim the counterexample is meant to illustrate.
Equality and inequality in the concrete claims are equalities and inequalities of whole grid functions; no separate extensional or pointwise formulation is named.
